solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Luvvie-like National player hogging musical's lead

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is wanted
a player hogging something keeps it wrapped up inside himself

blocks.note: a cap is a player picked for the national side

explanation.surface: A theatrical type of actor at the National hogs the limelight at the start of a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The M goes inside CA-P. A cap is a British sporting term for someone selected to play for their country.
explanation.definitionFit: Luvvies are gushing theatrical folk, and their manner is often called camp, meaning flamboyantly affected.

clue.text: Ejaculatory sound that gets you blessed?

definitions.text: Ejaculatory sound that gets you blessed?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cry at a sexual or religious climax
setter's reading: the noise of a sneeze, after which people say 'bless you'

explanation.surface: A smutty hint at a noise uttered in ecstasy that wins a blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ejaculatory' also just means suddenly exclaimed, and a sneeze is the sound that prompts 'bless you'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the conventional written spelling of a sneeze, the involuntary noise that people answer by saying bless you.

clue.text: Lay one on Brown, finally an ex-leader

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: to lay something down is to put it

explanation.surface: Someone thumps Gordon Brown, who is at last a former Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: At the time Putin had stepped down as Russia's president to become prime minister, hence ex-leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Putin had left the Russian presidency, so he counted as a former head of state at the time.

clue.text: Conservative arse preferred by parliamentary candidate?

definitions.text: Conservative arse preferred by parliamentary candidate?

blocks.note: conservative, as in cautious, is safe

explanation.surface: A Tory backside is what every would-be MP hopes to land.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines; a Conservative bum on the green benches suggests a seat a Tory cannot lose.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituency where one party's majority is so large that its candidate is certain to be elected is a prized prospect.

clue.text: Teaser showing peak of sizeable chest

indicators.note: the peak of a word is its top, its first letter in a down entry

blocks.note: a coffer is a strongbox or chest

explanation.surface: A tease flashes the top of an ample bosom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chest' wants to be anatomy here; it is the box.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who scoffs mocks or jeers, which is what a teaser does to the person being ribbed.

clue.text: (& 25dn.) Gay's mate needs puff before uninitiated bonk

indicators.note: uninitiated means without its initial, so the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: a fag is British slang for a cigarette, something to puff on
both are British slang for sex

explanation.surface: A gay man's partner wants a smoke before some lacklustre sex.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAG loses its S. The term is slangy and dated, and some find it offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase names a woman who mostly socialises with gay men, so she is a gay man's companion or friend.

clue.text: Drama as (making a comeback) Jack taken to heart by stricken nation

indicators.note: making a comeback is coming back, so the little word runs backwards
something stricken is damaged and out of shape, so its letters are scrambled
taken to heart puts one thing into the middle of another

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A troubled country takes a returning hero called Jack to its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drama' is the whole definition: the answer is a play by George Bernard Shaw. 'As' looks like a link word but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Joan is George Bernard Shaw's 1923 play, a drama about the trial and burning of Joan of Arc.

clue.text: Sporting type, Heath, unmanned, allowed at Maggie's end

indicators.note: unmanned means a man has been taken away, so a word for a male is removed
the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: Ted Heath, former Tory PM, taken as written

explanation.surface: Ted Heath, stripped of his manhood, plays sport while Thatcher finishes him off.
explanation.walkthrough: HEATH loses HE, the pronoun for a man. Heath and Maggie (Thatcher) were Tory rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a person who competes in sport, especially track and field events.

clue.text: see 11ac.
Very ring in which suitor screwed master

indicators.note: something screwed is twisted, so its letters come out of order
in which says the following letters sit inside the preceding pieces

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A seducer gets the better of the master of the house, within his very ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a performer of outstanding skill, a master of an art or instrument.

clue.text: Hostess offers messy shag, without that is, withdrawing

indicators.note: messy means disordered, so the letters are jumbled
withdrawing is pulling back, so the letters go the other way
without in its old sense means outside, so the jumble wraps round the rest

blocks.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A hostess offers a messy romp, then backs out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese woman trained to entertain and act as hostess to male guests.

clue.text: (& 8dn.) What the British electorate desperately needs? Could result in "Morgan event" (not 'A')

definitions.text: What the British electorate desperately needs?

blocks.clueFragment: What the British electorate desperately needs?
blocks.note: surface reading: a political verdict on the state of the country
setter's reading: rearranging the letters of the last word of the phrase yields the quoted words with their A removed

explanation.surface: A weary voter wants new rulers, and grumbles about some event involving a Morgan.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: shuffle the letters of GOVERNMENT, as the first two words instruct, and you get MORGAN EVENT minus its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters weary of the ruling party want it replaced, which is a switch in who runs the country.

clue.text: Labour leader has frothy latte (first entry of expenses!)

indicators.note: frothy suggests something whipped up, so these letters are churned
first entry is the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A Labour boss claims a frothy coffee on his parliamentary expenses.
explanation.walkthrough: A dig at the 2009 MPs' expenses scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee led the Labour Party for twenty years and was Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.

clue.text: Archer on? Be prepared for disgust

indicators.note: prepared means made ready by working on it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is Jeffrey Archer back on? Brace yourself for revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer is the Tory peer, novelist and jailed perjurer, a favourite Private Eye target.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrence is a feeling of strong loathing, so it is a near synonym for disgust.

clue.text: see 28ac.
Provisional number associated with Brown? Rubbish, Cyclops has possession

blocks.note: the PM lives at Number 10 Downing Street
the setter says I've, meaning I have, i.e. I possess

explanation.surface: A provisional figure tied to Gordon Brown is nonsense, says the setter, who holds the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyclops is the setter, so he is I; I'VE is I have, I possess.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tentative is offered provisionally, not yet settled or final.

clue.text: Hooker ran out holding tip of todger – what a state!

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
the tip of a word is its very first letter
holding means keeping something inside

explanation.surface: A prostitute flees, grasping the end of a man's member – what a to-do!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Todger' is British slang for penis. 'State' looks like 'what a state' meaning a mess; it is the country.
explanation.definitionFit: North Korea is a sovereign country in East Asia, and a country is a state.

clue.text: Darling opportunity to have a shag in retirement

indicators.note: retiring is going backwards, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: a roll in the hay is a shag

explanation.surface: A sweetheart sees a chance for a romp now he has retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' is not a term of endearment: Alistair Darling was Gordon Brown's Chancellor of the Exchequer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alistair Darling held the post of Chancellor of the Exchequer, Britain's finance minister, so his name stands for the office.

clue.text: Unhealthy as hard to get amount of blood nearly given by Hancock

blocks.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

blocks.clueFragment: amount of blood nearly given by Hancock
blocks.note: in Tony Hancock's sketch The Blood Donor he protests that a pint is very nearly an armful

explanation.surface: Losing nearly a pint of blood the way Hancock did is bad for your health.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Hancock was a British comedian; his famous line was 'That's very nearly an armful!'
explanation.definitionFit: Harmful means causing damage, and something unhealthy damages your health.

clue.text: Nautical mishap (one's lost nuts)

indicators.note: one being lost means a single letter for one, A, goes missing
a mishap is an accident, so the letters end up in disarray

explanation.surface: An accident at sea leaves someone's nuts missing.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two A's goes; A stands for one. 'Nuts' looks like the lost item but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is slang for mad, and a lunatic is a mad person; the definition is an adjective used loosely as a noun.

clue.text: Figure Brenda should be ditched – no feeling

indicators.note: ditched means thrown out, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A republican cry that the Queen should go, made without any emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye always calls Queen Elizabeth 'Brenda'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be numb is to be without sensation, so it matches having no feeling; the definition is a phrase used adjectivally.

clue.text: Rubber pack on Paris street upended

indicators.note: upended means turned upside down, which in a down entry reads the word bottom to top

blocks.note: a pack or crowd is a mass

explanation.surface: A condom packet is found on a Paris street, turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubber' wants to be a condom; it is someone who rubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur gives massages, rubbing the body, so he is literally a rubber.

clue.text: Brown: "Have to go, seat precarious" – tit!

indicators.note: to go means to be removed, so those letters leave the word
something precarious is unsteady, so its letters are tumbled

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown admits he must go as his seat is shaky, and is called a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: BROWN loses OWN. 'Tit' looks like an insult for Brown; it is slang for a breast.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit is slang for a woman's breast.

clue.text: Sex on cue: flopping is unpardonable

definitions.note: an adjective defining a phrase used predicatively: 'there is no excuse'

indicators.note: flopping means collapsing limply, so the letters fall in a new order

explanation.surface: Failing to perform when sex is expected is unforgivable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something for which there is no excuse cannot be justified or forgiven, which is what unpardonable means.

clue.text: Influence and power? Clegg at first gets left out!

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the named word

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Nick Clegg first gets shut out of influence and power.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats, perennially left out of power at the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Clout means political weight, the combination of sway and strength to get things done.

clue.text: Maybe Loach's aloof

blocks.note: first meaning: a loach is a small freshwater fish, so its things are, read as two words, of a fish

explanation.surface: The film director Ken Loach, perhaps, is standoffish.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as OF FISH. 'Loach' suggests the director Ken Loach; it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Offish is an informal word for standoffish, cool and distant toward other people.

clue.text: (see 5dn.)
Idle parasite, Darling, lacking will ultimately

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is removed
ultimately points to the final letter of the word

blocks.note: a tick is a bloodsucking parasite
darling and lover are both terms of endearment

explanation.surface: Alistair Darling is a lazy leech who has left no will.
explanation.walkthrough: LOVER loses its L. 'Darling' here is the endearment, not the Chancellor.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that ticks over is idling, running slowly without doing work.

clue.text: Over-sensitive, the French, dipping into pisspoor garlic

indicators.note: pisspoor means badly made, so these letters are jumbled
dipping into means going inside something

explanation.surface: The French, sensitive souls, dunking bread into dreadful garlic.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergic person's immune system overreacts to certain substances, so they are hypersensitive.

clue.text: (+ 13ac.) Rat's variety act put on film

blocks.note: a turn is a performer's act in a variety show
a film is a thin coat or layer

explanation.surface: A rat performs a variety act that gets filmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is read as 'is'. To rat is to desert your side.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is someone who deserts their party or friends, exactly what a turncoat does.
